products.name: Agent Home
products.need: Keep my agent’s identity and instructions portable
products.maturityDetail: Python wheel and source distribution are available.
products.purpose: Keep your agent’s identity, instructions, skills, and configuration in files you control, with local Git history.

taggedSetup.summary: Keep one agent’s instructions, skills, and configuration in a portable, Git-tracked home.
taggedSetup.requirements: Python 3.11+, Git, and a supported agent runtime to launch it.

does: Maps one portable agent definition into native configuration for pi, OpenCode, Codex, and Claude Code.
Keeps each home in a private local Git repository: commit changes, read the history, and restore earlier tracked contents as a new commit.
Refreshes native files from your edited Markdown with `soulsteads config <agent> --sync`.
Installs local skill directories, and can inspect and then optionally import selected Hermes profile files.
owns: The agent definition: identity, instructions, memory documents, skills, and learning preferences
Generated native configuration files inside the home
The home's tracked local Git history
doesNotOwn: Execution, native sessions, tools, or permissions: your harness keeps those
Harness installation, authentication, or global harness configuration
Models, gateways, scheduled jobs, or chat accounts
prerequisites: `uv` for the source install shown below
One supported harness (OpenCode, pi, Claude Code, or Codex), installed and authenticated separately
limits: Not a sandbox or a secret scanner: your harness keeps its machine permissions and can still load its own global configuration.
Start a new native session to load refreshed settings. Home-managed runs refresh the settings they own; native-only options remain harness-specific.
`soulsteads verify` is an offline structural check. It never launches an agent, so it does not prove that a harness loaded the configuration.

journey.title: Create a home and preview its launch

steps.title: Install the CLI, create a home, preview the launch command
steps.code:
uv tool install git+https://github.com/soulsteads/soulsteads-agent-home.git@2873e7d7b5d863a3463c452d8103331d3d1dedd7
soulsteads create helper --runtime opencode --path "$HOME/agent-home-example"
soulsteads verify "$HOME/agent-home-example"
soulsteads run "$HOME/agent-home-example" --dry-run

journey.after: Choose `pi`, `claude`, or `codex` instead of `opencode` if that is the harness you use. Once it is installed and authenticated, launch it with `soulsteads run "$HOME/agent-home-example"`.

products.name: Agent Messaging
products.need: Talk to my coding agent from chat
products.maturityDetail: Linux x86-64 archive available; source builds are also supported.
products.purpose: Use your existing coding agent from Telegram, Matrix, Mattermost, Slack, Discord, WhatsApp, or the built-in web interface.

taggedSetup.summary: Talk to an existing coding agent from chat or the built-in web interface.
taggedSetup.requirements: A supported, authenticated coding agent and connector credentials. Guided Telegram setup on Linux needs Git, Rust/Cargo, Python 3.11+, and a systemd user session. Set a nonempty sender allowlist before enabling a remote connector.

does: Runs on your machine and relays messages between your own chat account and the coding agent you already have signed in.
Includes connectors for Telegram, Matrix, Mattermost, Slack, Discord, WhatsApp, and a built-in web interface. Connectors are included, not preconfigured.
Works with Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, OpenCode, and Pi, or another compatible ACP server through a custom command. GitHub Copilot CLI is supported through native ACP.
Guided setup covers one path: Telegram with Claude Code or Codex on Linux. Every other combination is configured by hand.
owns: Bindings between chat conversations and agent sessions
doesNotOwn: Execution: the harness does the work, with its own permissions
Your terminal sessions: chat sessions are separate and terminal history is not transferred
Sandboxing, or a guaranteed stop for work that is already running
prerequisites: A coding agent (harness) that is already installed and signed in
A chat account and that connector's credentials, such as a Telegram bot token, kept in a private file
Rust/Cargo and Git to build the bridge from source
For the guided Telegram helper: Linux, Python 3.11+, and a systemd user session
limits: `/cancel` is not a kill switch. In the known Codex cancellation case a shell process can keep running, and unattended remote command execution is not qualified.
Telegram is not an end-to-end-encrypted connection to your machine. Matrix encrypted replies are not yet qualified for interoperability.
Approval prompts do not cover every tool: tools the agent already allows may run without another prompt.

Optional local agent tools (a build feature plus a runtime opt-in) let one conversation ask another already-attached agent in the same bridge process a question. Nothing is queued, there is no offline inbox, and there is no cross-machine transport. It is not a remote agent network.

journey.title: Connect an existing agent
journey.after: Follow the guide for the connector and runtime you actually use. Telegram setup is guided for Claude Code and Codex on Linux; other setups are manual. Start with a dedicated account and a harmless allowed-user prompt.

products.name: Agent Workboard
products.need: Give multiple agents one shared issue board
products.maturityDetail: Linux x86-64 archive available; source builds are also supported.
products.purpose: Give agents a shared issue board with dependencies, one active claim per issue, and a dashboard people can follow.

taggedSetup.summary: Coordinate issues, dependencies, and agent claims on a shared board.
taggedSetup.requirements: SQLite is bundled; no database server needed. A source build needs stable Rust and a C compiler.

does: A Rust issue board for agents: projects, epics, stories, tasks, and bugs, with dependencies, priorities, and acceptance criteria.
Gives each claim one owner: expiring leases, heartbeats, and tokens that reject stale workers. Required revisions stop silent overwrites.
Agents work through MCP, a JSON CLI, or an authenticated HTTP API. People follow progress in a live, read-only web dashboard.
One binary and one SQLite database. An optional idempotency key makes a retried change safe.
owns: The audit trail of which agent changed what
Per-agent API keys for access to the board
doesNotOwn: Execution: agents keep their own tools and do the work
External outcomes: a `done` issue is coordination state, not independent proof that something happened
Project-specific roles: keys identify agents in one trusted pool
prerequisites: Rust's stable toolchain and a C compiler (SQLite is bundled)
A checkout of the repository: the install command runs from it
Agents that can call a CLI, MCP, or HTTP
limits: Designed for one host that owns the SQLite database. Remote agents use HTTP; do not share the database file over a network filesystem.
`soulsteads-workboard web` listens on `127.0.0.1:7878` by default. Put any remote access behind an HTTPS reverse proxy.
API keys identify agents; they are not project-specific authorization roles. Any keyed agent can coordinate work across the board.
Changes are deduplicated only when you send an idempotency key. Without one, inspect state and events before retrying.

journey.title: Install it, create a board, open the dashboard

steps.title: Install from a checkout of the repository
steps.note: Use an absolute database path so every local process opens the same board. Its parent directory must already exist.
steps.code:
cargo install --locked --path .
export WORKBOARD_DB="$PWD/workboard.sqlite3"
export WORKBOARD_ACTOR="coordinator"

steps.title: Create a workspace
steps.note: Run these in a fresh database, with `WORKBOARD_API_KEY` unset.
steps.code:
soulsteads-workboard run '{"op":"agent_register","id":"coordinator","name":"Coordinator"}'
soulsteads-workboard run '{"op":"agent_register","id":"forge","name":"Forge","capabilities":["rust","tests"]}'
soulsteads-workboard run '{"op":"project_create","key":"AG","name":"Agent platform"}'
soulsteads-workboard run '{"op":"issue_create","project":"AG","kind":"epic","title":"Ship agent coordination"}'
soulsteads-workboard run '{"op":"issue_create","project":"AG","kind":"story","title":"Implement the work loop","parent":"AG-1","acceptance_criteria":["Integration tests pass"]}'
soulsteads-workboard run '{"op":"issue_transition","key":"AG-2","expected_revision":1,"state":"ready"}'

steps.title: Issue a key and open the dashboard
steps.note: Save the returned `api_key` privately; it is shown only once. Then open `http://127.0.0.1:7878` and enter that key.

journey.after: The ready story appears on the board, waiting for an agent to claim it. Leave the server running and connect a worker from another terminal or client.

products.name: Model Router
products.need: Give compatible clients one endpoint for existing models
products.maturityDetail: Linux x86-64 archive available; source builds are also supported.
products.purpose: Route compatible requests to existing model servers through stable aliases, per-client access rules, and shared capacity limits.

taggedSetup.summary: Route compatible requests to existing inference servers through one endpoint.
taggedSetup.requirements: An inference server and either Tailnet IPv4 or explicit loopback mode. A source build needs Rust/Cargo and a C toolchain.

does: Puts stable model aliases in front of your own inference servers, and restricts each client key to the aliases and routes it needs.
Checks declared capabilities and available capacity before choosing a backend, with bounded retries before any response is exposed.
Opt-in routing policies (rules or a local decision model) choose among explicitly authorized local, Codex, and Copilot aliases.
Shows health, admission, and request timing without logging prompt text by default.
owns: Request admission and placement across authorized routes
Client keys and what each key may reach
Shared capacity limits for the backends it fronts
doesNotOwn: The router does not host models or load them: bring an existing inference server
prerequisites: A Linux/Unix host with Rust/Cargo and a C toolchain
A running local OpenAI-compatible inference server whose exact model ID and tested limits you know
An assigned Tailnet IPv4 address in default mode, or explicit loopback mode for same-host clients. LAN and wildcard binds are rejected; port `4001` is reserved.
Python 3 for the setup guide's configuration and request examples
limits: Not a universal OpenAI drop-in. It exposes an OpenAI-compatible subset, and support depends on your exact backend and the capabilities you declare.
Serves HTTP without built-in TLS. Keep it on a protected network and do not expose it directly to the internet.
A routing policy never grants permission: cloud routes need explicit grants on the client key.
Optional passthrough mode bypasses managed capacity and safety checks. Leave it off unless you accept that different contract.

journey.title: Configure one model route
journey.after: Use an existing inference server with an exact model ID and verified limits. Validate the policy with `soulsteads-router --check-config` before starting. Configuration validation does not prove inference.

products.name: Agent Forge
products.need: Run recurring workflows and inspect what happened
products.maturityDetail: Linux x86-64 archive available; source builds are also supported.
products.purpose: Run one-off or recurring workflows, inspect step results, and recover carefully after an interruption.

taggedSetup.summary: Run and schedule workflows, then inspect their step results.
taggedSetup.requirements: Linux, a dedicated PostgreSQL database, and `jq` for the quickstart. Building from source also needs Rust 1.97+ and a C compiler.

owns: Workflow and schedule definitions, run history, and effect admission and receipts
doesNotOwn: Agent identity, issue and claim state, or model routing
Automatic undo or proof that an external effect happened
prerequisites: Linux, Rust 1.97 or later, and a C compiler
An empty, dedicated PostgreSQL database for DBOS
limits: Early release, not a production deployment claim. Listener is loopback only.
SQLite stores local admission and effect receipts; it is not a substitute for PostgreSQL.
Verify unknown external outcomes independently before retrying. Do not give untrusted executables access.

journey.title: Run a deterministic workflow
journey.after: Use the upstream quick start to initialize a fresh Forge home and run the sample workflow against a disposable PostgreSQL database. Check the output before adding a schedule, model, or plugin.

does: Runs typed workflows on demand or on a recurring schedule, with explicit time zones.
Shows runs, step output, failures, and the status of external effects through a local dashboard, CLI, authenticated HTTP, or stdio MCP.
Deterministic workflows need no model or harness. Configured models, harnesses, and trusted executable plugins are optional.

products.name: Agent Skillstore
products.need: Review, install, and recover agent skills
products.maturityDetail: Python wheel and source distribution are available. Linux tested; macOS qualification pending.
products.purpose: Share reviewed, versioned Agent Skills across projects and harnesses. Preview an update before installing it and recover previous versions offline.

taggedSetup.summary: Review, install, and recover versioned agent skills.
taggedSetup.requirements: Python 3.11+; tested on Linux. The local quickstart needs no model account, agent harness, or Agent Home.

does: Review an exact skill version and inspect the proposed file changes before installing.
Protect local edits and roll back or restore skills from local snapshots.
Use tracking-only mode for private skill backups without a registry.
prerequisites: Python 3.11 or later; use a release package or a source checkout with `uv` or `pip`
limits: The local quickstart needs no harness or model account.
Installation copies skill files without executing them.

journey.title: Try a local skill registry
journey.after: Follow the disposable quickstart to review, install, and recover a sample skill without changing your harness configuration.

guides.label: Back up skills without a registry

composition.title: Keep your harness. Run workflows separately.
composition.intro: Add tools to your existing agent only when you need them. You can also run Forge without connecting an agent.

steps.connection: Define the agent once in a home directory and generate native configuration for your harness.

Bridge a supported chat to an independently configured backend. Messaging's `acp.agentHome` sets a working directory, not an Agent Home import. Do not move existing session bindings as part of a fresh setup.
Give each agent the Workboard MCP server, CLI, or HTTP API, with its own key, to claim and hand off issues.
Point a compatible client at the router's endpoint, limited to the routes its key allows.
Run workflows on demand or on a schedule and inspect each step. The quick start works without a model or harness; harness-backed steps are optional.

notes: Products have separate installs, databases, and recovery paths. The setup helper prints a plan; it does not install anything.
limits: Messaging's local agent tools are a bounded exchange between already-attached agents in one bridge process on one machine. They are not a cross-machine agent network, and Soulsteads has no agent network product.

faq.q: Do I need the whole lineup?
faq.a: No. Every product is meant to be useful on its own; start with one and add another only if it helps. Independence does not mean no dependencies: Messaging needs a harness and a chat account, and Model Router needs an inference server. It means those needs never force you to adopt the rest of Soulsteads.

faq.q: Is this a hosted AI service?
faq.a: No. The published tools run on your machine. You bring your own harness, model access, chat accounts, and credentials. Your model and messaging providers' costs and privacy policies still apply.

No. Agent Home and Agent Messaging do not sandbox your agent: it keeps its machine permissions. Keep secrets out of tracked files, and use an account and workspace you are comfortable giving the agent.

faq.q: Can I cancel a remote task safely?
faq.a: Messaging's `/cancel` is not a kill switch. In the known Codex cancellation case a shell process can keep running, and unattended remote command execution is not qualified. Read the Messaging README before connecting a powerful agent.

faq.q: Can I bring an existing Hermes agent?
faq.a: Agent Home has an optional Hermes importer. Inspect an explicitly selected source first; applying creates a fresh home, not a live messaging cutover. Unsupported settings are reported, and incomplete imports need acknowledgement.

No. Messaging's optional local agent tools let one conversation ask another already-attached agent on the same machine a question, with nothing queued and no cross-machine delivery. A separate agent network is a possible future decision, not a product.

faq.q: Are binaries available, or do I build from source?
